nodes.label: DELETE /mock/rfq/:rfq_number
nodes.rationale: Delete cascades to every related record (QCF, tokens, logs) so a test run leaves no residue in the database.

nodes.label: Mock RFQ Scenario Templates
nodes.rationale: Named templates (pending_rfq, dual_vendor_pending, one_approved_one_pending, declined_scenario, cl_approved, complete_workflow) encode whole status combinations so a tester reproduces a workflow state without knowing the field-level rules.

nodes.label: DICConfirmationRequest schema
nodes.rationale: status_dic is optional when vendor status is NEED_CONFIRMATION because it is auto-set to REQUEST_REVISION; reject_reason becomes required for DECLINED, REQUEST_REVISION and NEED_CONFIRMATION items.

nodes.label: Business-Day Token Expiry Consistency
nodes.rationale: Weekends are excluded from every SLA query, token expiry and email deadline calculation. Calendar-day math silently shortened deadlines across weekends (Fri +3 landed on Monday), so vendors and DICs lost working days to respond.

nodes.label: Progressive Escalation Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Escalate gradually rather than failing fast: gentle reminder plus vendor_lvl2 activation at H+3, CS visibility at H+6, automatic hand-off to manual procurement at H+9, so vendor non-response never stalls a PR indefinitely.

nodes.label: dry_run validation mode
nodes.rationale: dry_run validates a payload without writing records, so a new scenario can be checked against the status rules before polluting the database.

nodes.label: Status Consistency Invariants
nodes.rationale: quotation_date is mandatory when status_vendor is ACCEPTED, status_dic cannot be ACCEPTED unless status_vendor is, and QCF may only be created at milestone 18 or 20 — so generated fixtures cannot represent states the real workflow can never reach.

nodes.label: clApproveItems - PUT /pr/cl/approve-items/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch}
nodes.rationale: Category Lead approval gate for RFQ items. The description explicitly names the action types it clears - 'surrogate, revisi_oe, etc.' - making it the shared terminus of the CS rfq_tipe dispatch actions. Addressed by rfq_number + vendor_batch; empty request-body schema. Bearer secured.

nodes.label: clApproveQCF - PUT /pr/cl/approve-qcf/{qcf_number}
nodes.rationale: Category Lead approval of a QCF, flagged '**Important**' because it is a side-effecting boundary: items are marked qcf_approved = true, vendor status updates are sent, and SAP Auto PO synchronization is triggered. This makes it the irreversible hand-off point from procurement review into SAP PO creation. Body carries an optional cl_comment. Bearer secured.

nodes.label: getNeedApprovalItems - GET /pr/cl/need-approval-items/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch}
nodes.rationale: Read side of the CL item-approval gate: retrieves RFQ items awaiting Category Lead approval, 'typically items with surrogate, revisi_oe, or special actions'. Bearer secured.

nodes.label: getNeedApprovalQCF - GET /pr/cl/need-approval-qcf/{qcf_number}
nodes.rationale: Retrieves QCF detail with cost-saving calculations for CL approval. Adds an optional vendor_code query filter that the token variant lacks. Bearer secured.

nodes.label: getNeedApprovalQCFByToken - GET /pr/cl/need-approval-qcf/token/{token}
nodes.rationale: Token-addressed twin of getNeedApprovalQCF with a byte-identical description, existing so an emailed approval link can resolve a QCF without the caller knowing the qcf_number. Bearer secured despite the token lookup.

nodes.label: getDeclinedItems - GET /pr/cs/declined-items/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch}
nodes.rationale: CS exception queue for vendor-declined RFQ items, defined by status_vendor = 2. Addressed by rfq_number + vendor_batch. Bearer secured.

nodes.label: getDeclinedItemsByToken - GET /pr/cs/declined-items/token/{token}
nodes.rationale: Token-addressed twin of getDeclinedItems. Selects RFQ items declined by the vendor via the magic constant status_vendor = 2.

nodes.label: getNotSubmittedItems - GET /pr/cs/not-submitted-items/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch}
nodes.rationale: CS exception queue for RFQ items a vendor has not yet submitted. Uniquely among the CS review reads it also accepts a vendor_code query filter, allowing a multi-vendor batch to be narrowed to one vendor before chasing them. Bearer secured.

nodes.label: getNotSubmittedItemsByToken - GET /pr/cs/not-submitted-items/token/{token}
nodes.rationale: Token-addressed twin of getNotSubmittedItems; same description, resolved from an emailed link rather than rfq_number + vendor_batch.

nodes.label: getOERevision - GET /pr/cs/oe-revision/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch}
nodes.rationale: CS queue of RFQ items pending Owner Estimate revision - the read counterpart to the rfq_tipe = 'revisi_oe' dispatch. Bearer secured.

nodes.label: getOERevisionByToken - GET /pr/cs/oe-revision/token/{token}
nodes.rationale: Token-addressed twin of getOERevision; identical description, differing only in how the RFQ batch is resolved.

nodes.label: getPriceNotMatch - GET /pr/cs/price-not-match/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch}
nodes.rationale: CS exception queue for items where the vendor price exceeds the OE threshold, compared against the item_value field. That same item_value is what sendRevisiOE rewrites, making this read the natural trigger for an OE revision. Bearer secured.

nodes.label: getPriceNotMatchByToken - GET /pr/cs/price-not-match/token/{token}
nodes.rationale: Token-addressed twin of getPriceNotMatch; same OE-threshold rule, resolved from an emailed link.

nodes.label: csResendRFQ - POST /pr/cs/resend-rfq/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch}
nodes.rationale: Manual CS resend of the RFQ email when a vendor has not confirmed receipt. The description explicitly cites a sibling operation: 'Same as /email/resend-request-for-quotation but requires BearerAuth instead of path parameters' - i.e. the duplication exists deliberately so the authenticated CS console can trigger the same send without exposing the unauthenticated email-token route. Empty request body.

nodes.label: rfqPreview - GET /pr/cs/rfq-preview-form/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch}
nodes.rationale: Renders RFQ form data for CS review before it is sent to the vendor - a pre-send verification step guarding the outbound email. Bearer secured.

nodes.label: sendIsourcing - POST /pr/cs/send-isourcing/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch}
nodes.rationale: Routes RFQ items into the iSourcing system for manual procurement, setting rfq_tipe = 'isourcing'. Explicitly justified as the escape hatch for 'complex procurement requirements that cannot be handled via standard RFQ workflow'. Its body example is the richest of the dispatch actions, carrying per-item sourcing_reason and sourcing_notes plus batch-level reason and notes - the audit trail for why automation was bypassed.

nodes.label: sendRevisiOE - POST /pr/cs/send-revisi-oe/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch}
nodes.rationale: Requests an Owner Estimate revision, setting rfq_tipe = 'revisi_oe'. Requires a new item_value per item - the same field getPriceNotMatch compares against - so this is the corrective action for an OE that was set too low.

nodes.label: sendSurrogate - POST /pr/cs/send-surrogate/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch}
nodes.rationale: Assigns a surrogate vendor to RFQ items, setting rfq_tipe = 'surrogate', and sends an email notification to the Category Lead for approval - so substituting a vendor is never unilateral, it always re-enters the CL approval gate.

nodes.label: sendToQCF - POST /pr/cs/send-to-qcf/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch}
nodes.rationale: The happy-path terminus of the CS stage: creates a Quotation Comparison Form from approved RFQ items, emails the CL for final approval, after which items proceed to SAP Auto PO synchronization. Unlike its sibling dispatch actions it declares a real typed schema with required items and rfq_tipe rather than an empty object.

nodes.label: getSurrogateItems - GET /pr/cs/surrogate-items/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch}
nodes.rationale: Lists RFQ items marked as surrogate for CS review - the read counterpart to the rfq_tipe = 'surrogate' dispatch. Bearer secured.

nodes.label: SendToQCF Request Body (items[] + rfq_tipe)
nodes.rationale: The only fully typed request body among the CS dispatch actions: an object requiring items (array of {id: integer}) and rfq_tipe (string). Its shape is echoed as untyped examples by sendSurrogate, sendRevisiOE and sendIsourcing, so it is the de facto contract for the whole rfq_tipe dispatch family and the candidate for extraction into components/schemas.

nodes.label: Bug 2 Premature DIC Email
nodes.rationale: In parallel mode the two vendors sit in different vendor_batch values after a DIC revise cycle, so a check scoped to the submitting vendor batch finds zero pending vendors and sends the DIC email while the sibling has not answered.

nodes.label: Bug 3 Need Action vs Waiting Vendor
nodes.norm_label: bug 3 need action vs waiting vendor
nodes.rationale: The S3 branch of toUserFlatRow followed milestone_id alone while the S1 and S2 branches already consulted sv_group, so a partially submitted parallel card claimed Need Action; the fix reuses data the query already returns instead of adding a subquery.

nodes.label: checkPendingRfqWithMultipleVendors
nodes.rationale: Asks whether two or more vendors are pending in one batch; both the batch scope and the threshold of two are wrong for parallel mode, where the real question is whether any sibling of the same item_code in the same sequence is still pending.

nodes.label: handleExpiredVendor Delay Mitigation
nodes.rationale: Holding an item back while a sibling is pending risks it never being sent; the expiry cron converts a silent vendor to RFQ_NOT_SUBMITTED, which removes the pending sibling and releases the DIC email.

nodes.label: shouldSendToDic Decision
nodes.rationale: A single boolean for the whole submission, so one waiting S3 item would otherwise also hold back the S2 items submitted alongside it.

nodes.label: sv_group Aggregate
nodes.rationale: MIN over status_vendor with ACCEPTED and NEED_CONFIRMATION folded to 1 yields PENDING whenever any grouped vendor has not submitted, which is exactly the sibling signal the dashboard needs.

nodes.label: Vendor Batch Divergence After DIC Revise
nodes.norm_label: vendor batch divergence after dic revise
nodes.rationale: vendor_batch increments before an item is re-sent, so repeated revise cycles leave the two parallel vendors in different batches; measured at 83 percent of S3 rows still matching, which is why the bug looked intermittent.

nodes.label: checkPendingVendorForItem
nodes.rationale: Per-item sibling check scoped by rfq_number, item_code and vendor_sequence, replacing a global two-vendor threshold that could not answer the parallel question.

nodes.label: Cross-Batch Pending Check for PARALLEL
nodes.rationale: The vendor_batch filter is dropped and the threshold lowered to one only when vendor_sequence is PARALLEL, so sequential flows keep their existing behaviour.

nodes.label: Per-Sequence DIC Dispatch Split
nodes.rationale: Items are grouped by vendor_sequence before dispatch so parallel items wait per item_code while S1 and S2 items keep the original shouldSendToDic path, and NEED_CONFIRMATION items stop being dispatched unconditionally.

nodes.label: Token vendor_batch Scoping Weakness
nodes.rationale: Tokens are scoped by a vendor_batch that mutates as items advance, so any token issued at batch N becomes permanently unresolvable once items move to N+1; scoping tokens by item ids is the durable fix, closing dead tokens is only mitigation.

nodes.label: has_sibling_manual_sourcing Flag
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes active manual sourcing (milestone 6 with tipe_rfq isourcing, which hides the sibling) from failed manual sourcing (milestone 12 with REJECTED, which does not).

nodes.label: parallel_covered_item_codes
nodes.rationale: Marks item codes already covered by an active sibling vendor in parallel mode so a rejected or expired vendor row is hidden from CS instead of demanding duplicate action.

nodes.label: toCsFlatRow Sibling Hide Rules
nodes.rationale: The pre-fix hide condition only suppressed aggregator rows, so a direct vendor stayed visible even when its sibling was already in manual sourcing.

nodes.label: vendor_sequence S1 S2 S3
nodes.rationale: Sequence 1 and 2 send the direct vendor then the aggregator in turn; sequence 3 sends both in parallel, which is why parallel needs its own hide/show rules.

nodes.label: Bug 1 DIC Detail Sequence Mixing
nodes.rationale: listItemRFQDIC filters on rfq_number, vendor_batch and statuses but never on vendor_sequence, so an S3 item grouped by item_code surfaces inside an S2 detail view; the dashboard query already had the exclusion logic the detail query lacked.

nodes.norm_label: bug 4 separate s3 cards without context
nodes.rationale: The dashboard GROUP BY emits one card per vendor state, so the same item code in the same sequence renders as two disconnected cards with no cross-vendor context.

nodes.label: vendor_sequence in DIC JWT Payload
nodes.rationale: The sequence must travel in the emailed token because the DIC detail endpoint is reached from a link with no session context; the filter stays optional so older tokens keep working.

nodes.label: Vendor Token-Based RFQ Access
nodes.rationale: The emailed JWT is checked for signature, presence in rfqTokenEmail, is_active and date_expired, and is deactivated on submission so a link cannot be reused.

nodes.label: items_wp Waiting Procurement Items
nodes.rationale: Mirrors s3DeclineHideFilter at the items-array level, excluding rows whose sibling is still active or accepted with DIC not final, so the card body agrees with the row-level filter.

nodes.label: listRfqUser Use Cases
nodes.rationale: One query drives the user and DIC dashboard; card identity is the combination of vendor_sequence, vc_group, dic_group, ms_group and cs_id, and card status follows the priority Need Action over Waiting Vendor over highest remaining milestone.

nodes.label: ms_group Milestone Grouping Key
nodes.rationale: Separates manual-sourcing items and OE-revision items from normal ones so a single vendor with mixed item states renders as distinct cards with correct labels.

nodes.label: needActionDicFilter
nodes.rationale: A card cannot demand DIC action when the DIC token is missing or expired, so those rows are dropped rather than shown as actionable.

nodes.label: s3DeclineHideFilter
nodes.rationale: In parallel mode with no DIC verdict yet, declined and expired vendors are hidden while any sibling is still active, so the card shows the live vendor rather than a dead one.

nodes.label: s3DicDeclinedHideFilter
nodes.rationale: Applies only when status_dic is non-null and DECLINED, which is why a null status_dic keeps the row visible.

nodes.label: seq1ExcludeFilter
nodes.rationale: An item that has moved to a later sequence must not also render under its earlier one, so sequence 1 and 2 rows are suppressed once the same item and vendor exist at sequence 3.

nodes.label: vc_group Card Grouping Key
nodes.rationale: Zero merges vendors into one card, the vendor_code splits them per vendor, and minus one collects declined and expired parallel vendors into a single Waiting Procurement card.

nodes.label: Vendor Expiry Definition via rfq_token_email
nodes.rationale: Expiry is decided by the latest token row for the vendor_code and vendor_batch, not by milestone 22 alone; a missing token row counts as expired.

nodes.rationale: Self-described backdoor endpoint requiring no authentication, kept for testing: it mints a JWT for an arbitrary rfq_number/type/vendor_code/vendor_batch with a caller-chosen expiresIn.

nodes.label: GET /pr/getAllRFQ (backdoor)
nodes.rationale: Documented as a backdoor with no authentication required and an explicit 'use with caution in production' warning; returns every RFQ record filtered only by status_vendor and vendor_batch.

nodes.rationale: Described only as an 'alternate format' of listRFQ with an entirely unspecified response schema; the parallel endpoint appears to exist for a differently shaped client payload rather than different data.

nodes.label: deleteSingleDocument (DELETE /upload/document)
nodes.rationale: Deletion is addressed by filePath in the JSON body rather than an id, matching the /uploads static-serving scheme where the stored URL is the canonical handle.

nodes.label: deleteMultipleFiles (DELETE /upload/files)
nodes.rationale: A single mixed-type delete endpoint that internally separates URLs by file type (image / document / evidence) and dispatches to the right deleter, so clients holding a heterogeneous attachment list need only one call.

nodes.label: Machine-readable error_code contract
nodes.rationale: 'Not authorized' and 'not found' are indistinguishable today (both 400 with the not-found message) and expiry vs malformed are both 403, so the frontend routes every failure to /page-expired; a machine-readable error_code lets it branch.

nodes.label: generateGemsManualPoLink
nodes.rationale: The existing token lookup keys on QCF number plus vendor code only, so writing a CS token today would overwrite the CL token row; the lookup must also match user_type and config_condition and store the CS token as a separate row.

nodes.label: Strict CS QCF token middleware
nodes.rationale: The existing middleware validates only JWT signature and expiry and never consults qcf_token_email, so revoked tokens keep working; the CS route additionally validates stored existence, is_active, stored expiry, stored purpose and matching qcf_number.

nodes.label: Shared Error Responses
nodes.rationale: Five reusable response objects (BadRequest, Unauthorized, Forbidden, NotFound, InternalServerError) all bound to the same ErrorResponse schema, so every endpoint documents failures identically.

nodes.label: Unbound QCF Token Risk
nodes.rationale: The QCF token payload carries only qcf_number, rfq_number and vendor_code, so it authorizes a QCF rather than a person; decodeTokenWithForbiddenException verifies only JWT signature and expiry and never consults qcf_token_email, so a revoked token keeps working until the JWT expires.

nodes.label: VendorSubmissionRequest Schema
nodes.rationale: Conditional-requirement design: vendor_price, quotation_number, vendor_description and vendor_delivery_date are required only when status_vendor=1 (ACCEPTED); vendor_reject_reason only when status_vendor=2 (REJECTED); vendor_description doubles as the vendor question when status_vendor=3 (NEED_CONFIRMATION). is_submit separates draft saves (0) from final submission (1), where only final submission triggers the DIC notification.

nodes.label: GET /autopo/{config_id}/available-values - Get Available Config Values
nodes.rationale: Exposes the allowed value set (for example plant_code values A100..G100) per config_condition so the UI renders a constrained dropdown instead of free text, keeping submitted config values valid.

nodes.label: GET /autopo/config/{configType}/{serverGroup}/{configCondition} - Get Active Config Value
nodes.rationale: Auto PO configuration is keyed by the triple (configType, serverGroup, configCondition), so the same condition such as skip_level_1_RFQ can carry different values per SAP server group (BCG vs GEMS).

nodes.label: GET /autopo/servers - List Auto PO Server Groups

nodes.label: POST /autopo/updateconfig/{id} - Update Configuration
nodes.rationale: Updates use POST rather than PUT/PATCH, matching the submit* naming convention used across the Auto PO Configuration tag.

nodes.label: POST /email/resend-failed - Resend Failed Emails
nodes.rationale: Failures are persisted in a FailedEmail table and retried with a hard cap of 5 retries, and the endpoint is designed to be driven by a cron job rather than by an operator, so transient SMTP outages self-heal without unbounded retry storms.

nodes.label: POST /email/resend-request-for-quotation/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch}/{vendor_code} - Manually Resend RFQ
nodes.rationale: Dual-vendor RFQs are modelled with vendor_batch 1 (primary) and 2 (secondary), where batch 2 is only processed if batch 1 declined; the endpoint therefore runs per-item dual-vendor validation before resending so a secondary vendor is not contacted prematurely.

nodes.label: POST /email/resend-rfq-by-vendor/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch}/{vendor_code} - Resend RFQ to Specific Vendor
nodes.norm_label: post /email/resend-rfq-by-vendor/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch}/{vendor_code} - resend rfq to specific vendor
nodes.rationale: Adds a request body carrying source_vendor_code and source_vendor_batch so items already quoted under one vendor batch can be re-targeted at a different vendor, which the plain resend-request-for-quotation variant cannot express.

nodes.label: POST /email/send-pr-received/{token} - Send PR Received Notification
nodes.rationale: The JWT token is decoded without validation for this operation, because the notification is purely informational to the PR creator and must still fire after the token's business-day expiry has passed.

nodes.norm_label: post /email/send-pr-revised-qcf/{itemids} - send pr revised to proceed to qcf
nodes.rationale: Takes a comma-separated list of item IDs in the path so one call can notify about a batch of revised RFQ items moving into QCF.

nodes.label: QCFA000731 Data Anomaly
nodes.rationale: A QCF number generateNextQcfNumber cannot produce, on rows whose qcf milestone disagrees with their rfq milestone, indicating the rows were edited outside the application; investigated and cleared as not a release blocker.

nodes.label: Dashboard SQL Views
nodes.rationale: Each role gets a paired list and summary view with status, status_group and action already derived from milestone_id, so callers filter on labels instead of re-deriving milestone semantics.

nodes.label: status_group Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Five buckets (need_action, waiting, manual_sourcing, po_published, not_awarded) collapse 25 milestones into the counters every dashboard summary reports.

nodes.label: Two-Year Data Window Filter
nodes.rationale: Every view restricts to the last two years so dashboard queries stay bounded as history grows.

nodes.label: Milestone-Strict PO Validation Trade-off
nodes.rationale: Requiring milestone 20 before showing PO Published would hide a genuine PO whose rfq milestone lagged, so the item-scoped fix is preferred over adding a milestone predicate.

nodes.label: Partial PO Within One QCF
nodes.rationale: The system cannot express a QCF whose items are only partly PO-issued, which is why a QCF number was edited by hand into a value the application cannot generate; proposed as a separate feature request.

nodes.label: status_milestone Field
nodes.rationale: A single numeric code carried by both rfqLibrary and qcfLibrary tracks workflow progression across 20+ states, so one column drives dashboards, filters and cron selection.

nodes.label: poPublishedSiblingHideFilter
nodes.rationale: Deliberately RFQ-wide rather than item-scoped because it exists to compute Not Awarded, which is a cross-item question.

nodes.label: importPRData (Step 1)
nodes.rationale: Skips PRs already present in rfq_library so existing PRs never re-enter the pipeline. This creates the 'lines that had a PO at import time never get an rfq_library row' gap, which was deliberately addressed at the iSearch read layer via the matrix_cs_aigen fallback rather than by changing the skip.

nodes.label: syncRFQData (Step 2)
nodes.rationale: Wrapped in a single DB transaction and ends with TRUNCATE TABLE pr_library, so re-running while a previous run is in progress is unsafe. Only groups whose summed value falls BELOW the config_auto_po threshold get an RFQ; above-threshold groups go the auto-PO route.

nodes.label: Log & SLA Gaps (Issue 1)
nodes.rationale: PR import, RFQ-number generation and CS/CL assignment are state changes that may belong in aigen.log_activity, but the worker writes nothing there today. Instrumentation should only be added where the user's own event mapping lists these transitions.

nodes.label: PR Ingestion Pipeline (3 Stages)
nodes.rationale: Documented explicitly because stage 2 (this worker) is routinely confused with stage 1 (Laravel SAP pull) and stage 3 (reminder-email cron); npm run run:cron in backend is a scheduler, not an importer.

nodes.label: aigen.pr_library Staging Table
nodes.rationale: Intentionally ephemeral: TRUNCATEd at the end of every successful syncRFQData cycle. Nothing that must be retained may live here; historical queries belong against rfq_library.

nodes.label: aigen.rfq_counters RFQ Number Allocation
nodes.rationale: Single-row counter (id 1) producing RFQ + 7-digit zero-padded numbers; centralising allocation in one row is what makes the duplicate-RFQ staging leak visible as a numbering anomaly.

nodes.label: Server-Group Value Column (BCG convert_value / GEMS value_idr)
nodes.norm_label: server-group value column (bcg convert_value / gems value_idr)
nodes.rationale: Each server group compares a different monetary column against the same threshold, so currency/normalisation differences between BCG and GEMS are handled by config rather than by branching code.

nodes.label: Duplicate RFQ Staging Leak
nodes.rationale: A throw inside _submitRFQ escaped before the TRUNCATE, stranding staging rows that merged into the NEXT run's new RFQ number. Symptom: the 2nd RFQ holds the prior run's items plus the new ones while the 1st RFQ is left with status_vendor NULL. Root cause was reading error.response.data on an undefined response during a network-level email failure; fixed 2026-06-15 by optional-chaining guards.

nodes.rationale: approveByCL branched on a feature flag before approvalConfig was consulted, so a flag silently cancelled Auto PO for QCFs whose stored config made CL approval final; every CL approval now flows through bulkApproveByCL which derives needsManagementApproval from the config.

nodes.label: GEMS_MANUAL_PO_FLOW Feature Flag
nodes.rationale: A pilot flag left active in production overrode stored configuration; the lesson recorded is that a feature flag must not be able to cancel a result already determined by configuration.

nodes.label: Milestone 26 Waiting Manual PO
nodes.rationale: Milestone 26 has no forward exit and bulkApproveByClForManualPo never calls syncAutoPO, so parked QCFs cannot self-heal and a retry is rejected as ALREADY_APPROVED.

nodes.label: Centralized Joi-Validated Configuration
nodes.rationale: All environment variables pass one Joi schema in config.js so a malformed value fails at boot instead of at first use.

nodes.label: K-1 CS Manual PO Confirmation
nodes.rationale: A per-QCF business confirmation, not a technical check: the scheduled SAP sync has been dead since 13 January 2026, so any existing PO can only have come from a manual CS action, making the CS answer the sole determinant of safety.

nodes.label: K-6 Re-Approval Method Decision
nodes.rationale: CL clicking in the app versus IT scripting the API against an admin token; bulkApproveByCL never writes cl_id, so the acting identity survives only in logActivity, which is why the choice is a business decision.

nodes.label: Step 4 QCF Status Rewind
nodes.rationale: Rewind runs one QCF at a time inside a transaction with a guard clause and only against QCFs CS has cleared as having no manual PO; a verified table backup is a hard precondition because this writes production data.

nodes.label: Step 5 CL Re-Approval
nodes.rationale: The point of no return: re-approval issues a real SAP PO, which AIGEN cannot cancel; it also requires the rewind first because the system rejects a repeat approval with ALREADY_APPROVED.

nodes.label: Duplicate PO Risk
nodes.rationale: Parking a QCF at Waiting Manual PO emails CS a live link instructing a manual SAP PO; re-approving such a QCF would create a second PO for the same purchase, and cancellation is only possible inside SAP.

nodes.label: syncAutoPO SAP PO Creation
nodes.rationale: Triggered by CL approval or by the sync cron; selects qcf_approved=1 with is_sync null or 0, posts a header/item payload whose document type, incoterms and tax code branch on server group, then writes back po_number, is_sync and the SLA lead time.

nodes.label: isourcing_transfer_requests Table
nodes.rationale: Stores business_key, origin_stage and an exhausted status so the attempt count is derived from stored state rather than defaulting to zero, which previously let a failed transfer block its PR forever.

nodes.label: Bug A DIC Expiry Without Manual Sourcing
nodes.norm_label: bug a dic expiry without manual sourcing
nodes.rationale: The reported RFQ was not blocked by code at all: the daily expiry job stopped running around 2026-07-25 and the token expired two days later; real code bugs found in the same job affect other RFQs.

nodes.label: 2026-07-25 Cron Schedule Outage
nodes.rationale: sourcing_reason stamps show four independent stages stopping within 72 hours of each other against an 08:00 WIB run history, and 15 tokens the old selection would have found sit unprocessed, which rules out an empty-but-running job and points at the schedule.

nodes.label: Duplicate PR to RFQ Root Cause
nodes.norm_label: duplicate pr to rfq root cause
nodes.rationale: The RFQ-creation job had no safeguard against re-processing the same PR item, so overlapping or repeated cron executions minted a second independent set of RFQ numbers for records that already existed.

nodes.label: Legacy Duplicate Cleanup Decision
nodes.rationale: Both sides of most duplicate pairs already carry tokens, uploads or a QCF, so choosing the surviving RFQ number is a business decision and cannot be scripted.

nodes.label: PR Item Vendor Uniqueness Guard
nodes.rationale: An existence check plus a database-level uniqueness rule on PR number, item code and vendor code makes recurrence impossible regardless of how often the cron overlaps.

nodes.label: Decision 3 Cron Stall Alert
nodes.rationale: Nothing notices when the automation stops, which is why the outage ran unnoticed for four weeks; this is the only change that prevents the reported bug recurring, since every other fix assumes the job runs.

nodes.label: continue-without-deactivate Bug Class
nodes.rationale: is_active=false is written only on the success path, so one non-200 pins a token as expired-and-active forever and every later run reproduces the same failure; the same shape is copy-pasted across the CL, Management and CS handlers.

nodes.label: CS Loop Null Guard
nodes.rationale: findOne returns null when a token RFQ row is gone and the property read sat outside any try/catch, so one orphaned token aborted the entire CS loop and silently skipped every remaining RFQ in that run.

nodes.label: excludeFinishedItems Finished-Work Guard
nodes.rationale: BA rule: an item that already carries a PO or is already iSourcing is finished, so close the token and do not process; a scope resolving to no rows also counts as finished, retiring orphaned tokens without sending email.

nodes.label: findItemsAwaitingDicReview
nodes.rationale: Replaces the cron round-trip through the HTTP controller and scopes from the token row own columns rather than the JWT, so a malformed token is no longer fatal, and selects on status_dic IS NULL instead of status_milestone = 3, which is the real business condition.

nodes.label: findQcfAwaitingApproval
nodes.rationale: Gated on a null approval timestamp, po_number IS NULL and a milestone not in the finished set; excluding finished states rather than whitelisting pending ones keeps future milestones safe by default and stops completed purchases being converted back to manual sourcing.

nodes.label: Sequence Drift Guard
nodes.rationale: A payload vendor_sequence that narrows the selection to zero is treated as a real failure rather than nothing-to-do, because closing the token there would silently discard pending work.

nodes.label: Decision 1 Eight Old Vendor RFQs
nodes.rationale: Processing April to June RFQs normally would send vendor and CS emails now, which looks like the system reviving dead work; the recommendation is to close them quietly.

nodes.label: Decision 2 CS Lookup Failure Retry
nodes.rationale: A failed sub-process is swallowed into an empty array, so nothing-to-do and check-failed are indistinguishable; retrying is safer but a permanently broken record then retries daily.

nodes.label: iSourcing database.driver
nodes.rationale: The pre-existing transfer logic moved verbatim out of qcfController so the default path is provably unchanged.

nodes.label: isourcingReconciliation.service
nodes.rationale: The API contract is a synchronous gate over asynchronous execution, so a transfer cannot report a final result in one call; a reconcile stage polls status, performs the deferred Aigen work on success, re-sends transient failures with a fresh idempotency key and escalates stale rows.

nodes.label: iSourcing Transfer Driver Layer
nodes.rationale: Transfers to iSourcing run behind a driver selected by one environment value so the existing direct-database mechanism stays the default while an API driver is developed; cutover becomes a config change rather than a code change.

nodes.label: isourcingTransfer.port
nodes.rationale: A single route into iSourcing that validates input, resolves the driver, guards the result shape, emits one structured log line per transfer and tags Sentry on failure, so no caller can bypass those invariants.

nodes.label: Pending Transfer Outcome
nodes.rationale: A third outcome beyond success and failure: while a transfer is only queued the RFQ token stays active and Aigen state is untouched, so nothing is committed against an unconfirmed transfer.

nodes.label: Business Day SLA Calculation
nodes.rationale: Token expiry and SLA tracking use business days rather than calendar days so weekends do not consume a vendor response window.

nodes.label: config_validation Thresholds
nodes.rationale: price_item_idr decides RFQ versus iSourcing routing; Max_price and Min_price bound price deviation; the two SLA day values drive every deadline in the flow.

nodes.label: iSourcing Manual Procurement Routing
nodes.rationale: High-value items and stalled RFQs leave the automated path into iSourcing board_card and item_card rows, auto-assigned to a CL by material group.

nodes.label: Health Endpoint Readiness Gate
nodes.rationale: The playbook polls /health up to 60 times before pruning old images so a failed rollout is not made unrecoverable.

nodes.rationale: Sentry alone cannot detect a job that never starts because the alert is emitted from inside the job; an externally monitored health endpoint is the only option that catches total stoppage.

nodes.rationale: A one-month pilot must revert by flipping one value with no redeploy, rollback migration or code change. An env var was chosen over config_autopo (read by the external import-pr cron, unverifiable risk) and over a feature_flags table (too much machinery). The cost is that toggling requires restarting both deployment units.

nodes.label: In-flight GEMS QCF Stranding
nodes.rationale: Eight GEMS rows sit CL-approved awaiting Management; once Management is blocked they become unreachable because CL cannot re-approve and the new path only fires at the moment of CL approval. Deploying with the flag off lets the backlog drain itself, avoiding any data migration.

nodes.label: Two Deployment Units Hazard
nodes.rationale: app.js and src/cron.js are separate processes with separate environments; if only one gets the flag, HTTP runs the pilot while cron still sweeps GEMS QCFs into Management expiry processing, and that failure is silent.

nodes.label: .deploy:docker_swarm Job Template
nodes.rationale: Runs ansible-playbook against deploy/${CI_COMMIT_BRANCH}.yaml, so the branch name selects the playbook; allow_failure is false because a silently failed deploy would leave the swarm on a stale image.

nodes.label: Import PR GitLab CI Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Only build and deploy stages are active; the test stage and the SonarQube CLI component are commented out, consistent with the repo having no automated tests.

nodes.label: Semeru Develop Deploy Playbook
nodes.rationale: gather_facts is disabled and DOCKER_TIMEOUT is raised to 600 because the playbook only issues docker service commands on dot_semeru and image pulls can exceed the default timeout.

nodes.label: Old Image Prune Task
nodes.rationale: ignore_errors is true so a prune failure never fails an otherwise successful deploy; disk hygiene is best-effort.

nodes.label: Docker Service Update Task
nodes.rationale: Uses docker service update --force on sinarmas-aigen-dev_import-pr rather than a stack redeploy, so only this one service is rolled; the health-check wait is commented out because the worker exposes no HTTP endpoint.

nodes.label: aigen-import-pr Container Image (hrbr registry)
nodes.rationale: Image tag is derived from CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA (develop{{sha}}), making every deploy traceable to an exact commit.

nodes.label: Note for Deployment Section
nodes.rationale: A standing hand-off channel to DevOps for out-of-band steps (migrations, file uploads, folder permissions, post-deploy SQL) that CI cannot infer from the diff; repeated verbatim across every MR template in the repo.

nodes.label: Rollback Mitigation Requirement
nodes.rationale: Unique to the refactor template: the author must pre-state the revert path (revert commit, rollback DB migration) before merge, because refactors have wide, non-obvious failure surfaces.

nodes.label: Bug Issue Template
nodes.rationale: Mandates login username, monitoring line/link and a cURL (via pastebin) so a developer can replicate an issue without going back to QA; title format is [Category/App/Module] Priority - Issue Overview.

nodes.label: New Feature Issue Template
nodes.rationale: Splits work into separate Backend and Frontend task checklists under one user story so a single feature issue can coordinate both sides, with acceptance criteria stated before tasks.

nodes.label: Default Merge Request Template
nodes.rationale: Explicitly instructs authors to describe behaviour ('Add auth feature') rather than the file list ('Create /controllers/auth.ts'), so reviewers read intent instead of a diff restatement.

nodes.label: MR-to-Production Template
nodes.rationale: Production MRs lead with Change Logs instead of an Issue reference and require a QA Testing Report link. Note: the Note for Deployment block is duplicated at L5 and L23 — an apparent copy-paste defect in the template.

nodes.label: Refactor Merge Request Template
nodes.rationale: Refactors change no behaviour, so the template demands per-consumer screenshot evidence ('Coverage and Evidences'), an explicit re-test list, and a declaration of potential issues — the reviewer cannot infer blast radius from the diff alone.

nodes.label: Up-to-Production MR Template
nodes.rationale: Minimal production promotion form: Change Logs, Note for Deployment, Testing Evidence — the same three sections as mr-to-prod-template but without the duplicated block.

nodes.label: CLI One-Shot Entry Point (app.js)
nodes.rationale: Runs the same two-step flow as the Kafka handler without needing Kafka; the npm alias aigen:import-pr does NOT forward --last-period-days, so lastPeriodDays silently falls back to LAST_PERIOD_SYNC.

nodes.label: Kafka Consumer Entry Point (worker.js)
nodes.rationale: Subscribes to KAFKA_TOPIC_IMPORT_PR (default aigen-import-pr-events) and shuts down gracefully on SIGINT/SIGTERM so in-flight DB transactions are not orphaned.

nodes.label: import-worker Compose Service
nodes.rationale: Runs npm run start:worker with restart: unless-stopped so the Kafka consumer survives crashes; the compose file defines only the worker because the CLI mode is invoked ad hoc.

nodes.label: External backend_network
nodes.rationale: Declared external and named from DOCKER_NETWORK_NAME so the worker joins a pre-existing network shared with Kafka, MySQL and the AiGen backend instead of creating an isolated one.

nodes.label: Sentry Init-Order Requirement
nodes.rationale: lib/sentry.js must be required before any other app module in every entry point so instrumentation hooks are installed before the modules they patch are loaded; any new entry point must preserve that ordering.

nodes.label: Cron Job Architecture
nodes.rationale: Every cron reminder is also exposed as a manual API endpoint so a single workflow can be re-triggered without waiting for the schedule.

nodes.label: Cron stage and rfq_number CLI Filter
nodes.norm_label: cron stage and rfq_number cli filter
nodes.rationale: runCronTasks already accepted stage and rfq_number options that no CLI could reach; parsing them lets a four-month backlog be drained in slices instead of firing every conversion, card and email at once.

nodes.label: Batched Backlog Drain Strategy
nodes.rationale: Four weeks of backlog would otherwise process in one run, creating iSourcing cards and CS emails for every stage at once.

nodes.label: Multi-Vendor Fallback lvl1 to lvl2
nodes.rationale: A declining or silent primary vendor must not stall the PR: decline duplicates the RFQ to vendor_lvl2 immediately, day 3 activates lvl2 on silence, and both silent at day 9 routes to iSourcing.

nodes.label: checkMultiVendorPending (GET /pr/rfq/check-multi-vendor-pending/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch})
nodes.rationale: Exists as a dedicated validation probe (has_multi_vendor_pending boolean) for the dual-vendor RFQ workflow so callers can branch before triggering escalation actions.

nodes.label: handle9DayFollowUp (POST /pr/rfq/handle-9-day-follow-up)
nodes.rationale: Nine days is the terminal point of the reminder ladder: if both vendors are still pending, items are auto-moved to iSourcing (manual sourcing) rather than waiting indefinitely for a quotation.

nodes.label: handleDeclinedPendingFollowUp (POST /pr/rfq/handle-declined-pending-follow-up)
nodes.rationale: Mixed declined/pending RFQs get separate notifications per status type so CS receives an unambiguous action per item rather than one blended message.

nodes.label: send3DayReminders (POST /pr/rfq/send-3-day-reminders)
nodes.rationale: At three days of vendor-1 silence the RFQ is duplicated for vendor 2 and emailed, so the secondary vendor is engaged early instead of only after the primary formally declines.

nodes.label: send6DayReminders (POST /pr/rfq/send-6-day-reminders)
nodes.rationale: Reminders are grouped by vendor before sending 'quotation not yet submitted' emails so a vendor with several pending RFQs receives one consolidated nudge.

nodes.label: Sourcing Reason
nodes.rationale: Reasons are stored as configuration rows carrying an actor field (e.g. 'cs') so the reason picker can be filtered per role; catalogued values cover price-above-OE, vendor-cannot-supply and vendor-did-not-submit.

nodes.label: Ansible Deploy Playbook - semeru develop stack
nodes.norm_label: ansible deploy playbook - semeru develop stack

nodes.label: _getPrVendorAndCSByVendorMatrixAssign
nodes.rationale: Annotated in source as '// old method, same on isourcing laravel app' — direct evidence that the legacy CS/CL resolution was copied across from the iSourcing Laravel app rather than rewritten.

nodes.label: ASSIGN_CS_CL_METHOD Runtime Switch
nodes.rationale: Both CS/CL resolution paths are kept alive behind an env flag (default material_assignment) so the vendor port retains parity with the iSourcing Laravel app during migration. Consequence: a bug fix to one branch must be evaluated against the other before it is deemed safe to skip.

nodes.label: internal/<feature> Branch Policy
nodes.rationale: Internal features are built on private internal/<feature> branches off the vendor's develop and are never pushed upstream, keeping the vendor-authored baseline cleanly separable from internal work.

nodes.label: Vendor Lineage Warning
nodes.rationale: aigen-pr-sourcing was supplied by an external vendor and dropped into the monorepo as a clone, not authored internally. It is a partial port of the iSourcing Laravel app rather than a clean-room rewrite, so it is unknown whether it replaced the legacy import endpoint, runs in parallel, or is scheduled in vendor production at all. Operational stance: treat upstream develop as authoritative and never assume a function is dead just because the alternative branch is enabled locally.

nodes.label: Three-Connection Database Fan-Out
nodes.rationale: Three logical MySQL connections against a single server: aigen (read + write), isearch (read-only), isourcing (read-only). The worker writes ONLY to the aigen schema; prpo and task_board are strictly read-only from here, which is what makes the read-side iSearch integration safe.

nodes.label: Project Structure Layout
nodes.rationale: Database query utilities are split per-schema under queries/aigen, queries/isearch and queries/isourcing, mirroring the three logical connections so a query can never accidentally cross schemas.

nodes.label: Connection Labels vs Real DB Names
nodes.norm_label: connection labels vs real db names
nodes.rationale: connection('isearch') actually targets prpo and connection('isourcing') targets task_board_27 (dev) / task_board (prod). Sequelize reads the real name from .env at runtime, so code need not encode the dev/prod split — only inline cross-DB SQL elsewhere in the repo does.

nodes.label: _getMaterialAssignment Cascade Resolver
nodes.rationale: Resolves to the most-specific level whose ROW EXISTS (material_number to extended_material_group to material_group), falling back to a parent only when the child row is absent. Existence, not vendor presence, drives the cascade so an intentionally vendor-less row can express 'manual sourcing' without being overridden by a parent.

nodes.label: _sendEmailRFQ
nodes.rationale: Error handling was rewritten to error.response?.data ?? error.message (2026-06-15) because a network-level failure returns no HTTP response, so reading error.response.data threw a TypeError that escaped syncRFQData before its TRUNCATE.

nodes.label: Main/Sub PIC N-Cardinality
nodes.rationale: If sub-CS becomes N-cardinality, categories_matrix and material_assignment resolution return multiple sub-CS users; today the code arbitrarily picks one (materialAssignment.sub_category), so the resolvers would need to return an array and persist all of them.

nodes.label: Manual Sourcing Opt-Out (null vendor)
nodes.rationale: A material_assignment row that exists but carries no vendor_direct and no aggregator returns null, meaning 'manual sourcing, do NOT import' — the PR deliberately stays in iSourcing. It must NOT fall back to the parent level, otherwise an explicit manual-sourcing decision would be silently overridden by a broader default.

nodes.label: CS Decision Matrix
nodes.rationale: Four exits from CS review (proceed to QCF, surrogate, revise OE, iSourcing) give a human a route out of every exception state rather than letting items dead-end.

nodes.label: DIC Confirmation Stage
nodes.rationale: The requesting department confirms the quotation before procurement acts; accept above the price threshold diverts to OE revision, decline routes to CS, and request-revision resets the vendor status and bumps vendor_batch.

nodes.label: PR to RFQ to QCF to PO Flow
nodes.norm_label: pr to rfq to qcf to po flow
nodes.rationale: One end-to-end pipeline with four roles (Vendor, DIC, CS, CL); all branches converge on SAP Auto PO creation, with manual iSourcing as the fallback for high-value or problematic items.

nodes.label: tipe_rfq Classification
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes the standard Auto PO path from isourcing, surrogate and revisi_oe exception paths without adding separate tables.

nodes.label: iSearch Missing PIC (Issue 2)
nodes.rationale: Resolved 2026-05-11 purely as a read-side change in prpoapi surfacing per-line PIC and a 2-state header (Completed / On Progress); no write-side code lives in this worker.

nodes.label: aigen.aigen_isourcing_source_data Live View

nodes.label: Multi-Role Identity Migration
nodes.rationale: Moves user identity to aigen.users plus user_matrices. Once it is the source of truth the legacy CS-to-CL lookup must switch its connection from isourcing to aigen and join user_matrices — or the legacy branch can be deleted outright if material_assignment becomes the only supported path post-rollout.

nodes.label: Abandoned prpo Write-Back Approach
nodes.rationale: The fix/aigen-pr-pic branch (2026-05-07 to 2026-05-11) added _writeAigenCsToSearchLibrary, _writeSourcingStatusHeader and _computeSourcingState to push PIC and state into prpo.search_library.aigen_cs_pic and prpo.sourcing_status. nodes.rationale: Unscoped, it closed every active token for the RFQ including DIC and vendor tokens for other batches; now scoped to the token vendor_batch and vendor_code.

nodes.label: generateDicSourcingLink Token Hijack
nodes.rationale: The lookup matches on rfq_number and vendor_batch only, so one token row can be taken over across vendors and stages; deliberately left unfixed because scoping it would leave a CS token active and create a new DIC row, changing which expiry job fires.

nodes.label: iSourcing User Migration
nodes.rationale: Users are copied from the iSourcing database into aigen_db before seeding, deduplicated by email plus username, to avoid seed conflicts.

nodes.label: Seeder Workflow
nodes.rationale: Seeders must be idempotent and include duplicate checks because they can be run repeatedly across environments.

nodes.label: GET /master/categories/levels (Get Category Levels)
nodes.rationale: Exposes the level enumeration (0 = category, 1 = sub-category) that the categories listing endpoint accepts as its level query filter.

nodes.label: POST /master/categories (Create Categories)
nodes.rationale: Accepts an array body rather than a single object so category/sub-category pairs can be seeded in bulk from master-data imports.

nodes.label: PUT /master/categories (Update Categories)
nodes.rationale: Array body requires id plus all fields; deactivation is expressed through the is_active flag instead of a delete operation.

nodes.label: GET /master/category-matrices (Category Matrix Pagination)
nodes.rationale: sort_by is documented as accepting joined columns (category.name, main_category_user.name, sub_category_user.name, leader_category_user.name, management_user.name), confirming the matrix row joins the category and four user roles.

nodes.label: POST /master/category-matrices (Bulk Create)
nodes.rationale: All five foreign keys (category_id, main_category_user_id, sub_category_user_id, leader_category_user_id, management_user_id) are required, so a matrix row is only valid when the full CS/CL/management approval chain is assigned.

nodes.label: GET /master/divisions (Get Division Pagination)
nodes.rationale: One of the few endpoints in this chunk with a fully typed response envelope (message + data.data[] + data.pagination), making it the reference shape for the shared pagination contract.

nodes.label: POST /master/divisions (Create Divisions)
nodes.rationale: Request schema is declared as an untyped object while the example is a JSON string containing an array, so the documented contract is weaker than the actual bulk-array behaviour.

nodes.label: DELETE /master/master-hierarchy/ (Duplicate Soft Delete, deprecated)
nodes.rationale: Duplicate of the deprecated DELETE in master_master-hierarchy.yaml, carried on the trailing-slash path variant.

nodes.label: PUT /master/master-hierarchy/ (Duplicate Update Material Hierarchy)
nodes.rationale: Byte-for-byte duplicate of the PUT defined in master_master-hierarchy.yaml, bound to a trailing-slash path variant; almost certainly an unintentional duplicate fragment rather than a distinct route.

nodes.label: DELETE /master/master-hierarchy (Soft Delete Material Hierarchy, deprecated)
nodes.rationale: Marked deprecated:true. Soft deletion of material group items is being retired in favour of the is_active flag carried on the create/update payloads, so referential history is preserved for existing RFQs.

nodes.label: GET /master/master-hierarchy (Material Hierarchy Pagination)
nodes.rationale: Unusually marks page, limit, search, sort_by and order as required:true, unlike the other master-data listings where the same parameters are optional.

nodes.label: POST /master/master-hierarchy (Create Material Hierarchy)
nodes.rationale: Creates material group items keyed by material_group, extended_material_group, material_number and server, establishing the SAP-side classification that vendor and category assignment later hangs off.

nodes.label: GET /master/master-hierarchy/server-groups (Server Group Scoped Hierarchy)
nodes.rationale: Separate route rather than an extra filter on the base listing, because server_groups and is_active are required here (multi-tenant SAP server scoping is mandatory) while they are optional on the unscoped listing.

nodes.label: DELETE /master/material-assignments (deprecated)
nodes.rationale: Marked deprecated:true and its request body is an exact copy of the update payload; deletion is superseded by the is_active flag on the update operation.

nodes.label: GET /master/material-assignments (Material Assignment Pagination)
nodes.rationale: Rows carry parent_id, server_groups, group_type (extended_material_group) and group_value, so a material assignment is a hierarchy node decorated with a direct vendor, aggregator vendors, a category and a sub-category. The declared response item schema instead describes user objects, which does not match the example payload.

nodes.label: PUT /master/material-assignments (Update Material Assignment)
nodes.rationale: There is no POST: assignment rows are materialised from the material hierarchy and only ever updated, which is why vendor_direct_id, category_id, sub_category_id and vendor_aggregator_ids are patched onto an existing id.

nodes.label: GET /master/material-assignments/server-groups (Server Group Scoped Assignments)
nodes.rationale: Parameter list and response example are identical to the unscoped material-assignments listing; the route exists to group results by SAP server group (BCG, GEMS, ECC) for the multi-server master-data screens.

nodes.label: DELETE /master/users (Delete Users)
nodes.rationale: Unlike categories, vendors and material data, users retain a real bulk delete that takes a plain array of integer ids rather than relying on an is_active flag.

nodes.label: GET /master/users/matrices (Get User Matrices Pagination)
nodes.rationale: Filterable by role_id, division_id and category_id, which is how admin screens answer 'who holds this role for this category'.

nodes.label: POST /master/users/matrices (Create User Matrices)
nodes.rationale: A user matrix binds user_id to role_id, division_id and a set of category_ids, with is_default marking the role a user lands on at login and is_admin granting elevated scope; this is the record the auth switch-role flow reads.

nodes.label: POST /master/users (Create Users)
nodes.rationale: Array body with name, email and type all required; type is a numeric enum (1 = INTERNAL, 2 = EXTERNAL) that separates staff accounts from vendor-side accounts.

nodes.label: GET /master/users/types (Get User Types)
nodes.rationale: Supplies the value/label pairs behind the numeric user type enum used on user create and update. The documented response schema describes full user objects instead of type objects, which looks like a copy-paste artefact from the users listing endpoint.

nodes.label: GET /master/vendors/{id} (Vendor Detail)
nodes.rationale: Documented example returns a paginated list of vendors rather than a single record, so the detail contract does not match its own example.

nodes.label: GET /master/vendors (Get Vendors Pagination)
nodes.rationale: Supports a server_groups filter because vendor master records are partitioned per SAP server group (BCG, GEMS).

nodes.label: POST /master/vendors (Bulk Create Vendors)
nodes.rationale: server_groups, number, email, city, street and is_active are all required, because vendor_email is the delivery address for RFQ and quotation emails and city/street are printed on generated documents.

nodes.label: No Autonomous Git Operations Policy
nodes.rationale: Users need full control over version control; autonomous commits can create unwanted history or push incomplete work.

nodes.label: AiGen Frontend App Logo (Vuetify V Mark)
nodes.norm_label: aigen frontend app logo (vuetify v mark)

nodes.label: POST /auth/login/basic - Basic Login
nodes.rationale: New-method login accepts a generic 'identifier' (email or username) instead of email only, and returns just an access_token with null level/role and empty permissions until a role is selected via switch-role.

nodes.label: POST /auth/login/oauth/google - Exchange Google OAuth Code
nodes.rationale: Authorization-code exchange is a separate POST from the URL-issuing GET so the browser redirect (/sso/callback.html) can hand the code back to the SPA, which then trades it for an access_token server-side.

nodes.label: POST /auth/login - User Login (Deprecated)
nodes.rationale: Tagged 'Authentication/Old method (Deprecated)'. Returns the full user object plus an array of roles inline because a single dashboard user may legitimately hold multiple roles (e.g. both CS and CL); the newer basic-login flow moved this multi-role resolution out of login and into /auth/me plus /auth/switch-role.

nodes.label: GET /auth/me - Get Current User Profile
nodes.rationale: Returns current_user, available_roles and a refreshed access_token together so the client can render a role picker without a second round trip.

nodes.label: PUT /auth/switch-role - Switch Active Role
nodes.rationale: Switching role re-issues the JWT with level, role and the resolved permission list embedded in the token payload, so downstream authorization reads permissions from the token rather than querying the ACL tables per request.

nodes.label: LoginResponse schema
nodes.rationale: Carries both the multi-valued roles/levels arrays and single-valued level/roles_id fields for backward compatibility; roles_id resolves to the higher role when a user holds both CS and CL.

nodes.label: bearer security scheme
nodes.rationale: JWT for dashboard users (CS/CL/DIC/Admin) obtained through the login endpoints; it is the default security applied to the whole spec.

nodes.label: emailToken security scheme
nodes.rationale: JWT embedded in email notifications for vendors and DIC users, validated against business-day expiry that excludes weekends; some endpoints accept it as a path parameter rather than an Authorization header.

nodes.label: Procurement Workflow Stages
nodes.rationale: The documented pipeline is PR creation, RFQ generation and vendor notification, vendor quotation submission, DIC confirmation, CS/CL approval, QCF generation, then SAP Auto PO synchronization; the tag taxonomy mirrors these stages by actor role.

nodes.label: AIGEN Backend API Bundled Spec
nodes.rationale: A single dereferenced build of the multi-file spec: every paths and components $ref is inlined so the document can be served to tooling that cannot resolve external file references.

nodes.label: bulkUpdateStatusRFQ
nodes.rationale: Updates rfq_library and qcf_library in one transaction with Promise.all, so a partial failure rolls both back; the milestone written depends on status_vendor (null yields MANUAL_SOURCING_FAILED, ACCEPTED yields ISOURCING, otherwise BID_MANUAL_SOURCING).

nodes.label: prosesToIsourcing
nodes.rationale: iSourcing uses a Kanban model: each PR becomes a board card that moves between lists, with PR items stored as item_card rows. If the card already exists only new items are appended, so re-running never duplicates a card.

nodes.label: Multi-Vendor Fallback Activation
nodes.rationale: Duplicating the RFQ for vendor_lvl2 at H+3 preserves competitive bidding when only one vendor was originally engaged, before the flow escalates to manual sourcing.

nodes.label: Post-iSourcing Token Deactivation
nodes.rationale: Once items enter iSourcing the vendor no longer needs the quotation page, so vendor and QCF tokens are deactivated to make already-sent email links unusable.

nodes.label: Vendor 2 Eligibility Validation (CS vs Admin)
nodes.rationale: If Vendor 1 already accepted an item, Vendor 2 must not be diverted for it. CS may only push Vendor 2 items when Vendor 1 declined, or when the reminder date has passed and Vendor 1 is still pending. Admin bypasses the check entirely and pulls Vendor 1 items in alongside, because Admin may move a whole RFQ at once.

nodes.label: GET /pr/listQCF (listQCF)
nodes.rationale: Scoped to the CL user and, unlike listPR and listRFQ which return a bare array, wraps its rows in a data/pagination envelope built from the shared PaginationMeta schema.

nodes.label: buildGemsManualPoRecipients
nodes.rationale: A new resolver is added rather than repurposing buildCsRecipients, which puts Sub CS in CC instead of To and is currently unused by any caller.

nodes.label: canApprove capability flag
nodes.rationale: canApprove is computed per endpoint today with two different formulas, so the same field name carries different semantics; moving it to per-authenticated-role is a behavior change the frontend must absorb.

nodes.label: canManualSourcing capability flag
nodes.rationale: Return role-aware capability booleans rather than raw fields so the GEMS rule does not have to be reimplemented in two codebases; the backend still enforces the rule server-side, making the booleans a rendering convenience rather than the security boundary.

nodes.label: cl_approved_at post-CL signal
nodes.rationale: cl_approved_at is the only field that means specifically 'CL approved'; it is destructured in the detail controllers but never placed in headerInformation, so exposing it is a required change.

nodes.label: GEMS Server Group Identification
nodes.rationale: server_groups is a stored per-QCF-row column copied at QCF creation from the RFQ row, never derived at read time, so it is stable and trustworthy. JS comparisons are strict equality with no normalization, so the frontend must match the exact string 'GEMS'.

nodes.label: MANAGEMENT_LABEL_MAP dashboard mapping
nodes.rationale: At CL_APPROVAL the Management map yields Need Action with action 'Approve / Manual Sourcing', so the default filter surfaces the GEMS row with action buttons rather than hiding it. That is the actual QA defect.

nodes.label: qcf_approved status flag
nodes.rationale: qcf_approved = 1 is set only after syncAutoPO succeeds, so it means 'PO published', not 'someone approved'; 2 means diverted to Manual Sourcing; null is the normal pending state. It cannot distinguish who approved and must not be used to detect the post-CL state.

nodes.label: WAITING_MANUAL_PO milestone 26
nodes.rationale: GEMS currently has no stable post-CL resting state because Auto PO immediately advances milestone 18 to SAP_SYNC_COMPLETE 20; a dedicated milestone 26 gives the Manual PO stage a durable state with po_number left null.

nodes.label: approveByCL GEMS branch
nodes.rationale: Reads the flag at approval time rather than from anything snapshotted at QCF creation, so in-flight QCFs follow whatever the flag says the moment CL clicks approve and no half-migrated population exists. The approval transaction commits before SMTP is attempted.

nodes.label: DASHBOARD_STATUS.WAITING_MANUAL_PO
nodes.rationale: A new dashboard status string rather than reusing 'Waiting CS', so seven role-scoped label maps and their milestone group arrays each need an entry or GEMS rows fall through unmapped.

nodes.label: findExpiredManagementReviewItems
nodes.rationale: Its predicate is 'CL approval done AND management_comment is null', which would sweep GEMS rows into Management expiry processing since the GEMS path mints no Management token; excluding GEMS is mandatory, not optional.

nodes.label: isGemsManualPoEnabled
nodes.rationale: Fail-closed and synchronous: unset, empty or unparseable resolves to off, because absence of configuration must never enable a pilot feature. Kept as the single read point so storage can move to a DB flag later without touching call sites.

nodes.label: normalizeEmailRecipients
nodes.rationale: Defense in depth for all existing email callers, not a substitute for the purpose-specific resolver; it changes behavior for every email in the system so it lands with its own tests.

nodes.label: qcfWorkflowPolicy
nodes.rationale: Centralizes the GEMS rules because GEMS behavior is currently only a side effect of seeded configuration; every function takes rows loaded from the database, never request body fields, and returns a structured result so callers can map 403 vs 409.

nodes.label: qcf_library.sub_category_id migration
nodes.rationale: Backfill must run before the FK or the constraint fails on pre-existing orphans; ON DELETE SET NULL rather than CASCADE so deleting a category cannot destroy QCF history. Dev probe shows only 2.3% of rfq_library rows carry the source value, so the feature would launch degraded.

nodes.label: WAITING_MANUAL_PO milestone 26
nodes.rationale: The dashboard mapping stays permanent even after rollback: the flag gates transitions, not interpretation, and rows that reached milestone 26 during the pilot have real Manual POs in SAP. It is terminal, since nothing writes po_number back.

nodes.label: Management Approval Eligibility Gap
nodes.rationale: PUT /pr/management/approve_qcf has a role guard but neither controller nor repository checks server group, approval config or prior CL approval; the update predicate is only qcf_number plus three null fields, so Management can approve a GEMS QCF before or after CL and trigger Auto PO.

nodes.label: Manual Sourcing Role Guard Gap
nodes.rationale: POST /pr/cs/send_isourcing has no role guard at all and the handler trusts a client-supplied is_system_action flag; worse, the iSourcing board mutation happens before the RFQ/QCF status updates, so a late rejection would leave an orphaned board card.

nodes.label: Missing qcf_library.sub_category_id Join Key
nodes.rationale: CS PIC resolution keys on category_matrices.category_id, but qcf_library has no sub_category_id column and insertBulkQcf copies only the sub_category name, so there is no key for any CS authorization or recipient resolution.

nodes.label: CL Ownership Filter Silently Drops
nodes.rationale: The controller passes a scalar cl_id where the repository expects an object with user_id and role, so user.user_id is undefined and the ownership predicate is never added; combined with the missing route role guard, any authenticated role reaches CL approval logic.

nodes.label: GET /pr/dashboard-cl (Dashboard CL)
nodes.rationale: QCF-centric dashboard for the Category Lead role. Filters are constrained to CL-relevant statuses (Waiting CL, Waiting Management, Manual Sourcing, PO Published, Not Awarded) and a single action 'Approve / Manual Sourcing', so the CL sees only decisions it can actually make.

nodes.label: GET /pr/dashboard-cs (Dashboard CS)
nodes.rationale: RFQ-centric dashboard for Customer Service. Rows are keyed by rfq_number + vendor_code + vendor_batch, so one RFQ appears once per vendor; actions offered are Resend RFQ / Manual Sourcing, >OE and Surrogate.

nodes.label: GET /pr/dashboard-management (Dashboard Management)
nodes.rationale: Same QCF row shape as Dashboard CL but adds cs_name/cs_email and drops the 'Not Awarded' filter, giving management full CS-plus-CL visibility over the same QCF records.

nodes.label: GET /pr/dashboard-user (Dashboard User)
nodes.rationale: Requester/DIC-facing RFQ dashboard. Carries dic_token in the payload so the row can deep-link straight into the token-based DIC confirmation screen, and exposes submission_deadline_remaining_days (which can go negative) for overdue tracking.

nodes.label: GET /pr/dashboard-vendor (Dashboard Vendor)
nodes.rationale: Response schema and example payload are byte-for-byte the same as Dashboard User; only the status_filter and action_filter enums differ (Submit RFQ / Request Revise), suggesting a shared query builder scoped by role.

nodes.label: GET DIC RFQ item list, auth-based (getDicRfqItemListAuth)
nodes.norm_label: get dic rfq item list, auth-based (getdicrfqitemlistauth)
nodes.rationale: Explicitly documented as the alternative to the token-in-URL version, for a DIC user already signed in to the dashboard: it uses the emailToken security scheme as a Bearer header rather than a path parameter, avoiding token leakage through URLs and browser history.

nodes.label: GET DIC RFQ item list by rfq_number + vendor_batch (getDICRFQItemsWithoutToken)
nodes.norm_label: get dic rfq item list by rfq_number + vendor_batch (getdicrfqitemswithouttoken)
nodes.rationale: Token-free variant of the DIC item list, addressed by path parameters instead of a JWT, with an optional milestone_id query filter so the same payload can be re-fetched for a specific workflow milestone.

nodes.label: GET DIC RFQ item list by email token (getDICRFQItems)
nodes.norm_label: get dic rfq item list by email token (getdicrfqitems)
nodes.rationale: Entry point reached from the DIC confirmation email: the JWT carrying rfq_number and vendor_batch is embedded in the path so the recipient needs no dashboard account.

nodes.label: PUT /pr/dic/konfirmasi-penawaran (dicConfirmQuotation)
nodes.rationale: DIC verdict is expressed as a numeric status_dic per item: 1 Accepted, 2 Declined, 3 Request Revision. Request Revision routes the RFQ back to the vendor rather than forward to CS, so the three-value encoding is what drives the branch in the downstream workflow.

nodes.label: POST /pr/generateTokenRFQ (backdoor, development only)
nodes.rationale: Development-only token minter supporting three token types (dic, vendor, management); returns not just the token but dateExpired, the decoded payload, a ready-made url and a usage block showing both the header form and the URL-access form, so a tester can jump straight into either the header-auth or the token-in-path endpoint.

nodes.label: GET /pr/get-test-data-rfq (Get List RFQ For Testing to DIC)
nodes.norm_label: get /pr/get-test-data-rfq (get list rfq for testing to dic)

nodes.label: POST /pr/getDetailPR (getPRDetail)
nodes.rationale: Uses POST with a pr_number body rather than a GET path parameter, unlike the sibling RFQ detail endpoint which takes rfqNumber as a query parameter.

nodes.label: PUT /pr/management/approve-qcf/{qcf_number} (mgmtApproveQCF)
nodes.rationale: Terminal approval step: setting qcf_approved marks items approved, pushes vendor status updates and triggers SAP Auto PO synchronisation, so this single call is the boundary between the AiGen workflow and SAP.

nodes.label: GET QCF needing management approval, by qcf_number (getNeedApprovalQCFForMgmt)
nodes.norm_label: get qcf needing management approval, by qcf_number (getneedapprovalqcfformgmt)
nodes.rationale: Dashboard-authenticated review screen; accepts an optional vendor_code query parameter to narrow a multi-vendor QCF to one vendor's offer.

nodes.label: GET QCF needing management approval, by token (getNeedApprovalQCFForMgmtByToken)
nodes.norm_label: get qcf needing management approval, by token (getneedapprovalqcfformgmtbytoken)
nodes.rationale: Email-link counterpart of the qcf_number variant, carrying the QCF number inside a JWT so an approver can open the review screen straight from a notification.

nodes.label: GET /pr/qcf-pending-approval (Get List QCF Pending For Testing)
nodes.norm_label: get /pr/qcf-pending-approval (get list qcf pending for testing)

nodes.label: Dashboard Summary Metrics
nodes.rationale: Every role dashboard returns the same counter block (total_*, total_items, need_action, waiting, po_published, manual_sourcing) plus a status_group discriminator on each row, so the frontend can render one shared summary-card component across all roles.

nodes.label: Quotation Deviation Analysis
nodes.rationale: Request-vs-offer comparison is pre-computed server side across quantity, price, subtotal, delivery_date, brand, warranty, delivery_address and address_details, each carrying raw values, a formatted string and a has_deviation flag, so reviewers see a consistent verdict instead of every client re-implementing the comparison.

nodes.label: emailToken Security Scheme
nodes.rationale: A second security scheme alongside 'bearer', used by endpoints reachable from emailed links so that vendors and DIC recipients can act without a dashboard account.

nodes.label: RFQ Test Scenario Payload
nodes.rationale: A dedicated QA payload bundling scenario (is_single_vendor, total_vendors, guaranteed_dic_link), token health (has_token, is_active, is_valid, hours_until_expiry, expires_at), items_summary counts and a per-item price_range, terminating in a ready_for_testing boolean, so testers can pick a valid fixture without querying the database.

nodes.label: QCF Cost Saving Calculation
nodes.rationale: baselineSpend is the owner estimate and actualSpend the awarded price, so actualSaving and savingPercentage go negative whenever the award exceeds the OE (the documented example shows -9.35%); the sign is the signal management is meant to act on.

nodes.label: GET /health (getHealth)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately declared unprotected (no bearer security block, unlike every other operation in this chunk) so load balancers and monitoring probes can reach it without credentials. Returns status, timestamp and uptime seconds.

nodes.label: DELETE /mock/rfq/{rfq_number}/delete (deleteMockRfq)
nodes.rationale: Development/testing-only cleanup counterpart to mock RFQ creation. Documented as permanently deleting the RFQ and all associated data, which is why the path parameter is constrained by the pattern ^RFQ[0-9]{7}$ as a guard against deleting arbitrary records.

nodes.label: POST /mock/rfq/batch (createMockRfqBatch)
nodes.rationale: Explicitly documented as development/testing-only. Bounded by count 1-100 to stop accidental mass data generation, and driven by a named scenario enum so testers request a workflow state rather than hand-building payloads.

nodes.label: POST /mock/rfq (Mock RFQ Library)
nodes.rationale: Fabricates a complete RFQ aggregate in one call (header, vendor batch, CS/CL assignment, line items with SAP material and plant data). The create_tokens, create_qcf, create_logs and dry_run flags exist so a tester can choose exactly which side effects occur without touching production import paths.

nodes.label: GET /mock/rfq/templates (getMockRfqTemplates)
nodes.rationale: Development/testing-only. Publishes the scenario catalogue (pending_vendor, pending_dic, pending_cs, pending_cl, completed, random) so the batch endpoint's scenario enum is discoverable and each template maps to a distinct stage of the RFQ approval workflow.

nodes.label: resendEmailToDIC (POST /pr/resend-email/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch})
nodes.rationale: Manual DIC confirmation email resend reuses the existing rfqTokenEmail token and only mints a new one when needed, so that operator-triggered resends do not invalidate the link already delivered to the DIC.

nodes.label: handleExpiredManagementReview (POST /pr/rfq/handle-expired-management-review)
nodes.rationale: Normally driven by the cron scheduler; exposed as a manual HTTP trigger specifically for testing and recovery when a scheduled run was missed or failed.

nodes.label: handleSingleSubmissionFollowUp (POST /pr/rfq/handle-single-submission-follow-up/{days})
nodes.rationale: The days path parameter is optional and falls back to a configured value so the same handler can serve both the scheduled cadence and ad-hoc replays at a different threshold.

nodes.label: notifySingleSubmission (POST /pr/rfq/notify-single-submission/{days})
nodes.rationale: When only one vendor has submitted by the deadline, the flow generates a DIC token and requests confirmation rather than blocking on the second vendor, keeping the RFQ moving toward QCF.

nodes.label: sendDICReminders (POST /pr/rfq/send-dic-reminders)
nodes.rationale: Runs daily and targets PR creators/requestors rather than vendors, because a stalled DIC confirmation is an internal bottleneck, not a vendor one.

nodes.label: getSapSlocList (GET /pr/sap/sloc/list)
nodes.rationale: Storage locations are fetched live from SAP scoped by plant code so PR/RFQ creation offers only SLOCs valid for that plant.

nodes.label: getVendorRFQItems (GET /pr/vendor/get/item/list/rfq/{token})
nodes.rationale: item_value (the OE price) is deliberately hidden in the vendor view for security so vendors cannot anchor their bid to the internal owner's estimate; the JWT is taken from the path and validated against the rfqTokenEmail table. The payload also carries a per-field deviations block comparing request vs offer (quantity, price, subtotal, delivery date, brand, warranty, delivery address, address details).

nodes.label: getVendorRfqItemListAuth (GET /pr/vendor/get/item/list/rfq/{vendor_code}/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch} auth)
nodes.rationale: Alternative to the URL-token variant that authenticates with a Bearer emailToken, used when the vendor is already signed in to the dashboard so the flow does not depend on an email link.

nodes.label: getVendorRFQItemsWithoutToken (GET /pr/vendor/get/item/list/rfq/{vendor_code}/{rfq_number}/{vendor_batch})
nodes.rationale: Addresses the same vendor RFQ view by explicit vendor_code / rfq_number / vendor_batch instead of an email token, for callers that already know the identifiers; the response schema is identical to the token variant.

nodes.label: getRevisedRFQ (GET /pr/vendor/revisi/rfq)
nodes.rationale: Serves the DIC-revision branch of the vendor flow, gated on status_dic = 3 (REQUEST_REVISION), so vendors resubmit only the items the DIC sent back.

nodes.label: vendorSubmitQuotation (PUT /pr/vendor/submit/penawaran)
nodes.rationale: Price is checked by maxPricevalidation() against min/max percentage thresholds and out-of-range items land in rejectedForPrice rather than failing the whole submission. Vendor 2 items are only processed when Vendor 1 declined that specific item, preserving dual-vendor precedence at item granularity. On a complete submission the endpoint mints a DIC token and returns dicLink so the confirmation email can be dispatched immediately.

nodes.label: uploadSingleDocument (POST /upload/document)
nodes.rationale: Constrained to 10MB and PDF/DOC/DOCX/XLS/XLSX; requires rfq_number and vendor_code in the multipart body so every document is bound to an RFQ-vendor pair at upload time.

nodes.label: uploadSingleEvidence (POST /upload/evidence)
nodes.rationale: Evidence is keyed to rfqItemId rather than rfq_number so proof attaches to the individual line item under negotiation; 10MB cap per file.

nodes.label: uploadMultipleEvidences (POST /upload/evidences)
nodes.rationale: Batch variant capped at 5 files of 10MB each; the multipart field is named images even though the route is the evidence route, so callers must not assume field name follows resource name.

nodes.label: ErrorResponse schema
nodes.rationale: message is a oneOf string-or-array so a single general error and a Joi validation error list share one envelope; data is always null on errors.

nodes.label: StandardResponse schema
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the sendResponse(res, data, message, status) helper so every successful payload is wrapped in the same message plus data envelope.
